findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares the abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and (newly added in this PR) `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because the class implements none of them it remains abstract, so `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Previously the handler was concrete (it implemented `evaluate` returning `[]`), so this is a runtime regression for metric alert detector processing. Either keep a concrete stub implementation or don't register the handler until it is implemented.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the return type was changed in this PR to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Misleading documentation for implementers of the new handler contract.

findings.title: Multi-group test passes the wrong value for group_2 and still passes
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, `group_vals` contains `{"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}` but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with `value=6`. The test only passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores the `value` argument, meaning the test does not actually verify that the detector passes the correct per-group value into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Use the real value (10) and have the mock incorporate `value` (e.g. in `evidence_data`) so the hook's arguments are actually asserted.

findings.title: No test covers producing a StatusChangeMessage through process_detectors
findings.body: `process_detectors`/`create_issue_occurrence_from_result` has two branches: `PayloadType.OCCURRENCE` and `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE`. Only the occurrence branch is exercised (`test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`). The resolve path, which sends `payload_type=PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` with `occurrence=None`, is never asserted end-to-end, so a regression in the status-change produce call would go unnoticed. The previously existing duplicate-group-key test was also removed without an equivalent assertion that duplicate keys are now impossible by construction.
